ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.

ElementDescription: Sex of subject at birth
Notes: M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported

ElementDescription: Timepoint/visit label
Notes: e.g., Baseline, 6-Month Follow Up, Year 2; Morning, At Bedtime

ElementDescription: As you know, your doctor recently prescribed you an antidepressant medication for symptoms of depression. How long ago did the current depression symptoms start?
Notes: Time in years, months, days or weeks

ElementDescription: Have you started taking the antidepressant medication that you were recently prescribed?
How many days has it been since you started taking this antidepressant?
[ONLY IF PARTICIPANT HAS NOT STARTED MED] Think about whether it is likely or unlikely that you will start taking this antidepressant at some point during the next ten days? Would you say that it is:
Notes: 1= Very likely; 2 =Slightly likely; 3= No opinion; 4= Slightly unlikely; 5 = Very unlikely

ElementDescription: [ONLY IF PARTICIPANT HAS NOT STARTED MED] Sometimes doctors recommend trying antidepressant medications for at least 6 weeks. If you begin taking this medication, how likely is it that you will continue to take it until your doctor recommends that you stop? Is it:
Notes: 1= Very likely; 2 =Slightly likely; 3= No opinion; 4= Slightly unlikely; 5 = Very unlikely

ElementDescription: [ONLY IF PARTICIPANT HAS STARTED MED] Sometimes doctors recommend trying antidepressant medications for at least 6 weeks. Think about whether it is likely or unlikely that you will continue to take the antidepressant until your doctor recommends you stop? Is it:
Notes: 1= Very likely; 2 =Slightly likely; 3= No opinion; 4= Slightly unlikely; 5 = Very unlikely

ElementDescription: Please think about the care you received for this episode of depression from your primary care provider. How would you rate your involvement in decisions about your care?
How concerned are you about negative consequences of taking antidepressant medication?
Notes: 1=Very Concerned; 2= Moderately Concerned; 3= Somewhat Concerned; 4=A little concerned; 5=Not at all concerned

ElementDescription: How old were you when you first had symptoms of depression?
Before this antidepressant, have you ever taken an antidepressant medication for symptoms of depression?
Not including the antidepressant medication you were recently prescribed, when was the last time that you took an antidepressant medication?
How satisfied were you with that antidepressant?
Notes: 1=Very satisfied; 2= Satisfied; 3 =Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied; 4= Dissatisfied; 5=Very dissatisfied

ElementDescription: Have you ever in your lifetime received counseling or therapy from a mental health professional such as a psychiatrist, psychologist, psychiatric nurse, or clinical social worker?
Are you currently receiving counseling or therapy from a mental health professional?

Have you ever in your lifetime been admitted for an overnight stay in a hospital or other facility to receive help for problems with your emotions, nerves, mental health, or your use of alcohol or drugs?

Have you ever in your lifetime been admitted for an overnight stay in a hospital or other facility to receive help for problems with your emotions, nerves, mental health, or your use of alcohol or drugs? If yes, how many times in your lifetime has this occurred?
